text.p: Five pitchers combined on a five-hitter and pinch-runner Miguel Mejia scored the go-ahead run from second on a sacrifice bunt in the top of the ninth inning as the St. Louis Cardinals blanked the Los Angeles Dodgers 2-0 for their 11th win in 14 games Friday.

Starter Todd Stottlemyre gave up two hits before he was struck below the right knee by a line drive off the bat of Todd Hollandsworth in the sixth. Stottlemyre was taken to a Los Angeles-area hospital for precautionary X-rays.
St. Louis regained a 2 1/2-game lead over second-place Houston in the National League Central.
In Chicago, Steve Trachsel allowed two runs in seven innings and Dave Magadan had a two-run double in the first inning as the Chicago Cubs managed a 4-2 win over the Philadelphia Phillies.
Chicago won for the fourth time in five games.

Trachsel (12-8) allowed eight hits and no walks with four strikeouts for his first win in five starts. the fourth inning with an undisclosed ailment. Mike Winter, who started the game umping second, took over behind the plate as the game finished with three umpires.

At Colorado, Dante Bichette hit his 30th homer to become the the 16th player in baseball history to reach the 30-30 milestone and the Colorado Rockies became the first team to have four 30 home-run hitters in consecutive seasons as they defeated the Houston Astros 6-3.

Bichette, who has 30 stolen bases, homered off Astros starter Shane Reynolds in the sixth inning, knotting the game 3-3. He joins teammates Andres Galarraga, Ellis Burks and Vinny Castilla, who had previously reached the 30-homer mark.
In Montreal, Rondell White's RBI single snapped a sixth-inning tie and Pedro Martinez allowed one earned run over 6-2/3 innings as the Montreal Expos edged the Florida Marlins 3-2.
Henry Rodriguez and Shane Andrews homered for Montreal, which won for the 10th time in 14 games and moved within one-half game of San Diego for the National League wild-card berth.
In New York, Rey Ordonez had an RBI double in the bottom of the eighth inning and scored on Lance Johnson's single as the New York Mets handed the Atlanta Braves their fifth straight loss 6-4.
Bernard Gilkey went 3-for-3 and drove in two runs for the Mets. Ordonez is 6-for-16 with five RBI in his last five games.

In San Diego, Mike Morgan allowed three hits over six scoreless innings and Hal Morris homered and drove in two runs as the Cincinnati Reds continued their dominance over the San Diego Padres with a 3-1 victory.
The Reds posted their seventh straight win over the Padres and have taken nine of 10 meetings this season.
"We've had our tough times against the Reds," added Padres manager Bruce Bochy. "Some things are hard to explain. That's one of them."

In San Francisco, Esteban Loaiza tossed his first career shutout and Jeff King belted his third grand slam of the season to lead the Pittsburgh Pirates to a 9-0 rout of the San Francisco Giants in a battle of last-place teams.
Loaiza (1-2) scattered six hits, struck out five and walked two for his second complete game of the season.
